finding.description: Describes a defect in the same-role review, not a candidate defect already captured by a supported review finding.

reviewFindingAdjudication.description: Judges one finding made by the same-role review rather than judging the candidate defect again.

findingIds.description: Links only adjudicator findings that explain why this review finding is rejected; this array is empty when judgment is supported.

surfaceAdjudication.description: Echoes the bound same-role review assessment in reviewAssessmentJudgment and judges the soundness of that assessment in judgment. A sound blocking review assessment is blocking plus supported, not an adjudication failure.

findingIds.description: Links only adjudicator findings that explain a rejected same-role review assessment. It is empty for supported; rejected requires a linked blocking finding on this surface.

judgment.description: supported approves the same-role review assessment even when reviewAssessmentJudgment is blocking; rejected means the assessment is unsound or incomplete.

reviewAssessmentJudgment.description: Exact echo of the bound same-role review assessment's judgment; the deterministic verifier rejects any mismatch.

adjudicationSchema.description: This record judges the soundness and completeness of the same-role review, not the candidate.

findings.description: Adjudicator findings describe defects in the same-role review's requirement, assessment, reasoning, finding, coverage, or severity; they do not repeat candidate defects already captured by supported review findings.

reviewFindingAdjudications.description: Each entry judges one same-role review finding. A supported review finding has no adjudicator-finding links; a rejected review finding requires a linked blocking adjudicator finding that explains the review defect.

surfaceAdjudications.description: Each entry exactly echoes the same-role review assessment's pass, advisory, or blocking judgment, then separately judges that assessment as supported or rejected; it does not judge the candidate surface directly.

verdict.description: pass means the same-role review is sound and complete, even when that review correctly fails the candidate; fail means the same-role review is unsound or incomplete. This verdict never judges the candidate directly.

adjudicationSchema.title: Independent canonical-English semantic adjudication record

adjudicationSemantics.failMeaning: The same-role review is unsound or incomplete.
adjudicationSemantics.findingLinkMeaning: A supported surface assessment or review finding has no adjudicator-finding links; a rejected one links at least one blocking adjudicator finding on an overlapping surface that explains a defect in the review.
adjudicationSemantics.passMeaning: The same-role review is sound and complete, even when that review correctly fails the candidate.
adjudicationSemantics.subject: same-role-review
adjudicationSemantics.surfaceAdjudicationMeaning: Each surface adjudication exactly echoes the bound review assessment judgment in reviewAssessmentJudgment, then uses judgment supported or rejected to judge that assessment.

The problem: changes need a fixed comparison point The previous chapter joined the tokenizer, decoder, training, evaluation, checkpoint and generation code. Now the course will extend that system. If the data, configuration and code change together, a changed result no longer tells you which version you observed. You need a fixed reference that identifies its inputs and states exactly what its checks establish. This chapter keeps the small scalar decoder unchanged. It gives that reference an input identity and a report whose claims stay attached to their evidence. The identity identifies the fixed inputs. The checks establish which behavior this execution reproduced. Neither establishes useful laptop-scale capability.
What the reference actually does The fixture assigns 8 documents to training, 2 to validation and 2 to test. The decoder has 1188 learned scalar parameters and context capacity 4 tokens. Its primary training schedule and separately executed replay each perform 32 updates on full batches of 16 windows, with 4 valid targets per window. Therefore, each schedule consumes 32\cdot16\cdot4=2048 valid training targets. One pipeline invocation includes both schedules: 4096 targets altogether. These counts are derived from the frozen full-batch schedule, not from a new runtime token counter. Evaluation targets and generated tokens are separate quantities. The report’s independent_schedules field counts two separately executed copies of the same schedule from training seed 39, not statistically independent seed samples. The replay agrees bit for bit with the primary training result in this execution. The selected decoder and frozen bigram then score the same 1744 overlapping test-window target slots. Their mean negative log-likelihoods are approximately 3.866087547 and 3.981342714 nats per slot, respectively. This known comparison is a regression check: rerunning it can expose changes in the checked behavior. It is not an independent estimate of generalization. There are only 442 within-document transition occurrences in those test documents. Overlapping windows repeat occurrences, so 1744 is not a count of distinct transitions. A separate policy would score each occurrence once, using the longest available causal prefix capped at four tokens and only its newest-position distribution. This run does not report numeric mean NLL or perplexity under that policy. The checkpoint round trip preserves its encoded bytes, model and optimizer bits, and tokenizer. The restored decoder reproduces logits for the fixed At probe, encoded as token IDs [67,118]. Cached and complete-prefix generation agree on token IDs [260,34,34]: Cyrillic т followed by two spaces. Agreement checks the two generation paths; those three tokens do not demonstrate useful language quality.
The solution: identify inputs, then interpret evidence R_{\mathrm{ref}}=\operatorname{SHA256}(\mathrm{config}_{1188}\Vert\mathrm{fixture}\Vert\mathrm{source\_revision})
The identity’s symbols and fixed settings R_{\mathrm{ref}} is a 256-bit digest, displayed as 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. Its three named inputs are: \mathrm{config}_{1188}: a canonical record of eighteen tiny-run settings, together with the invariant that the decoder has 1188 parameters. \mathrm{fixture}: a canonical record of SHA-256 digests of the exact corpus bytes and exact split-manifest bytes. Even a byte change that leaves parsed JSON meaning unchanged creates a different input identity. \mathrm{source\_revision}: a verified source identity combining a baseline revision with the exact forty course-owned scalar-reference source files. Here \Vert means composition into the shared identity format’s named, canonical fields, not writing three unframed strings beside one another. That distinction matters: without field boundaries, different input sequences can have the same concatenated bytes. The helper orders fields, serializes one unambiguous record and hashes its complete bytes. The settings fix eight BPE merges; decoder width, feed-forward width and context capacity of four; one attention head and one block; stride one; training and evaluation batch sizes of sixteen and one hundred twenty-eight; thirty-two updates; learning rate 0.04; gradient-norm cap 1; training seed 39; generation seed 38; bigram smoothing 1; generation temperature 0.8; top-k four; and three generated tokens. The identity records floating-point settings by their exact bit patterns rather than rounded display text. Bind configuration, exact fixture bytes and verified scalar-reference source to one input identity. rust/demos/ch40-reference-core-handoff/src/lib.rs#reference-input-identity /// Bind every tiny-config field, including exact represented floating values. /// The count is the reference decoder's required 1,188-parameter invariant. pub fn tiny_config_identity() -> Result<ArtifactIdentity, IdentityError> { let config = CapstoneConfig::tiny(); let fields = [ ("parameters", "1188".to_owned()), ("bpe_merges", config.bpe_merges().to_string()), ("model_width", config.model_width().to_string()), ("heads", config.heads().to_string()), ( "feed_forward_width", config.feed_forward_width().to_string(), ), ("layers", config.layers().to_string()), ("context_length", config.context_length().to_string()), ("window_stride", config.window_stride().to_string()), ("update_batch_size", config.update_batch_size().to_string()), ( "evaluation_batch_size", config.evaluation_batch_size().to_string(), ), ("updates", config.updates().to_string()), ( "learning_rate_f64_bits", format!("{:016x}", config.learning_rate().to_bits()), ), ( "max_gradient_norm_f64_bits", format!("{:016x}", config.max_gradient_norm().to_bits()), ), ("seed", config.seed().to_string()), ("generation_seed", config.generation_seed().to_string()), ( "bigram_alpha_f64_bits", format!("{:016x}", config.bigram_alpha().to_bits()), ), ( "generation_temperature_f64_bits", format!("{:016x}", config.generation_temperature().to_bits()), ), ("generation_top_k", config.generation_top_k().to_string()), ("generation_tokens", config.generation_tokens().to_string()), ]; ArtifactIdentity::new( "scalar_reference_config", fields.iter().map(|(key, value)| (*key, value.as_str())), ) } /// Pure identity construction, also usable by mutation tests without training. /// An identity by itself does not admit alternate inputs to the reference run. pub fn reference_input_identity( config: &ArtifactIdentity, corpus: &[u8], splits: &[u8], source: &ArtifactIdentity, ) -> Result<ArtifactIdentity, IdentityError> { let corpus_digest = sha256(corpus); let splits_digest = sha256(splits); let fixture = ArtifactIdentity::new( "scalar_reference_fixture", [ ("corpus_sha256", corpus_digest.as_hex()), ("splits_sha256", splits_digest.as_hex()), ], )?; let config_bytes = canonical_string(config)?; let fixture_bytes = canonical_string(&fixture)?; let source_bytes = canonical_string(source)?; ArtifactIdentity::new( "scalar_reference_run", [ ("config_1188", config_bytes.as_str()), ("fixture", fixture_bytes.as_str()), ("source_revision", source_bytes.as_str()), ], ) } The example verifies its compiled reference-source evidence first. It then rejects changed corpus or split bytes before training or checkpoint work. Only accepted fixed inputs reach the existing pipeline. The wrapper calls that pipeline once; the pipeline itself performs primary training and replay. Reject changed fixtures, run the unchanged scalar pipeline and retain only its checked observation. rust/demos/ch40-reference-core-handoff/src/lib.rs#reference-handoff /// Refuse changed fixtures before model/checkpoint work, then call the existing /// capstone once. That call already includes primary training and full replay. pub fn run_reference_handoff( corpus_source: &str, split_source: &str, checkpoint_path: impl AsRef<Path>, source: &ReferenceSourceProof, ) -> Result<ReferenceHandoffTrace, ReferenceHandoffError> { if sha256(corpus_source.as_bytes()).as_hex() != CORPUS_SHA256 { return Err(ReferenceHandoffError::FixtureMismatch("corpus")); } if sha256(split_source.as_bytes()).as_hex() != SPLITS_SHA256 { return Err(ReferenceHandoffError::FixtureMismatch("split manifest")); } // Safe callers obtain this opaque proof only through the foundation's // approved-manifest/compiled-census verification, not a revision string. let identity = reference_input_identity( &tiny_config_identity()?, corpus_source.as_bytes(), split_source.as_bytes(), source.identity(), )?; let digest = identity.digest()?; let observation = run_capstone( corpus_source, split_source, checkpoint_path, CapstoneConfig::tiny(), )?; let evaluation = observation.final_evaluation(); let checkpoint = observation.checkpoint(); if observation.training().parameter_count() != 1188 || observation.training().optimizer_step() != 32 || !observation.training().replay_bitwise() || evaluation.window_count() != 436 || evaluation.window_target_slot_count() != 1744 || evaluation.document_transition_occurrence_count() != 442 || !evaluation.decoder().mean_nll().is_finite() || !evaluation.bigram().mean_nll().is_finite() || !checkpoint.bytes_roundtrip() || !checkpoint.model_bits_exact() || !checkpoint.optimizer_bits_exact() || !checkpoint.tokenizer_exact() || !checkpoint.prompt_logits_bitwise() || !observation.generation().tokens_exact() || !observation.generation().decisions_bitwise() || !observation.generation().rng_state_exact() { return Err(ReferenceHandoffError::Invariant( "scalar reference handoff evidence changed", )); } Ok(ReferenceHandoffTrace { identity, digest, source_revision: source.source_revision().to_owned(), observation, }) } What matching identities do not prove A matching digest identifies the same canonical input record, subject to the hash’s collision-resistance assumption. It does not prove that the algorithm is correct or that a new machine will reproduce every floating-point bit. The source identity deliberately covers the forty scalar-reference source files, not this chapter’s reporting wrapper or interface. Toolchain, locked dependencies and arithmetic environment are recorded separately. A matching source digest is therefore not evidence that two execution environments match. The temporary checkpoint path is also outside the input identity; changing that path does not change the model’s fixed inputs. Likewise, exact checkpoint reload is narrower than complete job resumption. This check does not restore every data cursor, in-flight operation or whole-job continuation state. No laptop throughput is measured here.
History: reporting conditions and measuring variation A language-model score without its input conditions and scope does not identify what was evaluated or establish which capabilities were checked. Model Cards for Model Reporting was presented in 2019. Mitchell and colleagues propose model documentation that includes intended uses and evaluation conditions; a model card is not itself proof of quality. Model Cards describe evaluation conditions and intended uses; later fine-tuning experiments study variation across initializations and data orders. Reporting scope and measuring variation answer different questions. In Fine-Tuning Pretrained Language Models: Weight Initializations, Data Orders, and Early Stopping, published in 2020, Dodge and colleagues study fine-tuning variability associated with initialization and data order for pretrained language models. This does not measure variability in the course’s tiny decoder. Keep a fixed regression reference when changing an LLM pipeline, while recording separately the evidence needed for quality, seed sensitivity and hardware claims. The Rust reporting contrast uses the same observation. Reading only the mean NLL with this expression gives a number: trace .observation() .final_evaluation() .decoder() .mean_nll() trace.report() also states the evaluation unit, input identity, replay accounting and limits. It does not retrain a historical model or execute a seed sweep. Report the same scalar observation with its metric unit, input identity and explicit capability limits. rust/demos/ch40-reference-core-handoff/src/lib.rs#scope-bearing-report /// Read structured evidence from this one observation; never parse stdout /// or run another model to produce either reporting projection. pub fn report(&self) -> Result<String, ReferenceHandoffError> { let run = &self.observation; let evaluation = run.final_evaluation(); let checkpoint = run.checkpoint(); let generation = run.generation(); let config = CapstoneConfig::tiny(); let targets_per_schedule = config.updates() * config.update_batch_size() * config.context_length(); let record = serde_json::json!({ "schema_version": 1, "chapter": "40-reference-core-handoff", "reference_identity": self.digest.as_hex(), "source_revision": self.source_revision, "scope": "scalar-reference-fixed-fixture-regression", "documents": { "train": run.partitions().train_document_ids().len(), "validation": run.partitions().validation_document_ids().len(), "test": run.partitions().test_document_ids().len() }, "model": { "parameters": run.training().parameter_count(), "context_tokens": config.context_length() }, "training": { "target_count_basis": "derived-from-frozen-full-batch-schedules", "updates_per_schedule": config.updates(), "independent_schedules": 2, "valid_targets_per_schedule": targets_per_schedule, "valid_targets_primary_plus_replay": 2 * targets_per_schedule, "selected_step": run.training().selected_step(), "within_invocation_replay_bitwise": run.training().replay_bitwise() }, "evaluation": { "unit": "overlapping-window-target-slot", "windows": evaluation.window_count(), "window_target_slots": evaluation.window_target_slot_count(), "document_transition_occurrences": evaluation.document_transition_occurrence_count(), "transition_multiplicity_counts": evaluation.transition_multiplicity_counts(), "decoder_mean_nll_nats_per_slot": evaluation.decoder().mean_nll(), "bigram_mean_nll_nats_per_slot": evaluation.bigram().mean_nll(), "once_per_transition_metric_reported": false, "independent_generalization_estimate": false }, "checkpoint": { "bytes_roundtrip": checkpoint.bytes_roundtrip(), "model_bits_exact": checkpoint.model_bits_exact(), "optimizer_bits_exact": checkpoint.optimizer_bits_exact(), "tokenizer_exact": checkpoint.tokenizer_exact(), "logit_probe_text": checkpoint.logit_probe_text(), "logit_probe_ids": checkpoint.logit_probe_ids(), "probe_logits_bitwise": checkpoint.prompt_logits_bitwise(), "complete_job_resume_established": false }, "generation": { "prompt": generation.prompt_text(), "token_ids": generation.generated_ids(), "decoded_text": generation.decoded_text(), "cached_reference_tokens_exact": generation.tokens_exact(), "cached_reference_decisions_bitwise": generation.decisions_bitwise(), "cached_reference_rng_exact": generation.rng_state_exact(), "useful_language_quality_established": false }, "laptop_throughput_measured": false, "successor_chapter": SUCCESSOR_CHAPTER }); let mut text = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&record) .map_err(|_| ReferenceHandoffError::Serialization)?; text.push('\n'); Ok(text) } Repeating seed 39 checks repeatability under fixed conditions. It does not estimate variability across seeds. Those are complementary checks, not interchangeable evidence.
Run the reference without changing its inputs The example obtains verified source evidence and owns its temporary checkpoint location. Its report comes directly from the checked scalar observation, not from parsing a previous human-readable report. Verify the reference source, use an owned temporary checkpoint and print the scope-bearing report. rust/demos/ch40-reference-core-handoff/src/main.rs#reference-example fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> { let source = verify_compiled_reference_source()?; let checkpoint = OwnedCheckpoint::new()?; let trace = run_reference_handoff(CORPUS, SPLITS, &checkpoint.file, &source)?; print!("{}", trace.report()?); Ok(()) }
Keep the three evidence layers separate The digest identifies the fixed inputs. The counts and generated token IDs describe checked behavior on those inputs. The final card keeps future quality, job-resumption and hardware claims outside the reference’s evidence boundary. A reference identity is not a capability certificate The configuration, exact corpus and split bytes, and verified scalar-reference source determine the input identity. Separate checks observe replay, fixed-window evaluation, reload and cached generation. Neither the identity nor those checks establishes useful language quality, complete job resumption or laptop throughput. Identify the fixed inputs SHA-256 identity of the fixed input record cd06104ff61dc8a0c6cbe6e842847952343050eb4942c79aa1d17e8d0d0bb648 Learned scalar parameters 1188 Read the checked reference behavior Overlapping test-window target slots 1744 Within-document transition occurrences 442 Generated token IDs [260,34,34] Keep unmeasured capabilities separate Not established: useful language quality, complete job resumption or laptop throughput.
Optional practice: inspect the boundary Run the example and inspect its report: cargo run --quiet --locked -p ch40-reference-core-handoff Find the identity, target-count basis and metric unit in the output. Explain why a digest alone would not replace the replay and reload checks. Run the demo’s tests. Identify the tests that change configuration, corpus, split bytes and source identity without training. Explain why constructing an identity for changed inputs does not admit them to the fixed reference run. Explain why a successful checkpoint round trip cannot justify the statement “the complete training job can resume,” and why 1744 must not be labeled “distinct test transitions.” Answers: input identity, evidence scope and repeated target slots The digest binds inputs; replay and reload compare actual behavior. Neither kind of evidence substitutes for the other. The target-count basis explicitly derives 2048 targets per schedule and 4096 for primary plus replay. The reported mean NLL uses nats per overlapping window-target slot. The pure mutation tests construct different identities without calling the pipeline. The runner separately requires the exact accepted corpus and split bytes, so an identity is not an admission permit. The checkpoint check covers persisted model, optimizer and tokenizer state plus a fixed logit probe, not every whole-job continuation dependency. The 1744 denominator counts overlapping window-target slots; the underlying documents contain 442 transition occurrences.
What the next extension must preserve You now have an identified scalar reference and a precisely bounded report. A later change can be compared with that reference, while carrying its own input identity and evidence. Chapter 41 will address governed corpus acquisition. New data, larger models, accelerator execution, quality evaluation and complete job resumption each require their own checks; none is already established by this handoff.

<h2 id="the-problem-changes-need-a-fixed-comparison-point">The problem: changes need a fixed comparison point</h2>
<p>The previous chapter joined the tokenizer, decoder, training, evaluation,
checkpoint and generation code. Now the course will extend that system. If the
data, configuration and code change together, a changed result no longer tells
you which version you observed. You need a fixed reference that identifies its
inputs and states exactly what its checks establish.</p>
<p>This chapter keeps the small scalar decoder unchanged. It gives that reference
an input identity and a report whose claims stay attached to their evidence.
The identity identifies the fixed inputs. The checks establish which behavior
this execution reproduced. Neither establishes useful laptop-scale capability.</p>
<h3 id="what-the-reference-actually-does">What the reference actually does</h3>
<p>The fixture assigns <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">8</span></span></span></span> documents to training, <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">2</span></span></span></span> to validation and <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">2</span></span></span></span> to test.
The decoder has <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>1188</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1188</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">1188</span></span></span></span> learned scalar parameters and context capacity <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">4</span></span></span></span> tokens.
Its primary training schedule and separately executed replay each perform <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>32</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">32</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">32</span></span></span></span> updates
on full batches of <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">16</span></span></span></span> windows, with <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">4</span></span></span></span> valid targets per window. Therefore,
each schedule consumes</p>
<span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><mn>32</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>2048</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">32\cdot16\cdot4=2048</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">32</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2222em"></span><span class="mbin">⋅</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2222em"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">16</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2222em"></span><span class="mbin">⋅</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2222em"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">4</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">2048</span></span></span></span></span>
<p>valid training targets. One pipeline invocation includes both schedules: <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>4096</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4096</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">4096</span></span></span></span>
targets altogether. These counts are derived from the frozen full-batch
schedule, not from a new runtime token counter. Evaluation targets and generated
tokens are separate quantities.</p>
<p>The report’s <code>independent_schedules</code> field counts two separately executed copies
of the same schedule from training seed <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>39</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">39</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">39</span></span></span></span>, not statistically independent
seed samples.</p>
<p>The replay agrees bit for bit with the primary training result in this
execution. The selected decoder and frozen bigram then score the same <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>1744</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1744</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">1744</span></span></span></span>
overlapping test-window target slots. Their mean negative log-likelihoods are
approximately <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>3.866087547</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.866087547</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">3.866087547</span></span></span></span> and <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>3.981342714</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.981342714</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">3.981342714</span></span></span></span> nats per slot, respectively.
This known comparison is a regression check: rerunning it can expose changes
in the checked behavior. It is not an independent estimate of generalization.</p>
<p>There are only <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>442</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">442</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">442</span></span></span></span> within-document transition occurrences in those test
documents. Overlapping windows repeat occurrences, so <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>1744</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1744</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">1744</span></span></span></span> is not a count
of distinct transitions. A separate policy would score each occurrence once,
using the longest available causal prefix capped at four tokens and only its
newest-position distribution. This run does not report numeric mean NLL or
perplexity under that policy.</p>
<p>The checkpoint round trip preserves its encoded bytes, model and optimizer
bits, and tokenizer. The restored decoder reproduces logits for the fixed
<code>At</code> probe, encoded as token IDs <code>[67,118]</code>. Cached and complete-prefix generation
agree on token IDs <code>[260,34,34]</code>: Cyrillic <code>т</code> followed by two spaces. Agreement
checks the two generation paths; those three tokens do not demonstrate useful
language quality.</p>

<h2 id="the-identitys-symbols-and-fixed-settings">The identity’s symbols and fixed settings</h2>
<p><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">f</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{\mathrm{ref}}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.8333em;vertical-align:-0.15em"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0077em">R</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.3361em"><span style="top:-2.55em;margin-left:-0.0077em;margin-right:0.05em"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mathrm mtight" style="margin-right:0.0778em">ref</span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.15em"><span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span> is a <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>256</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">256</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">256</span></span></span></span>-bit digest, displayed as <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>64</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">64</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">64</span></span></span></span> lowercase hexadecimal
characters. Its three named inputs are:</p>
<ul>
<li><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">f</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mrow><mn>1188</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{config}_{1188}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.9386em;vertical-align:-0.2441em"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathrm" style="margin-right:0.0139em">config</span></span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.207em"><span style="top:-2.4559em;margin-right:0.05em"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight">1188</span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.2441em"><span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span>: a canonical record of eighteen tiny-run settings,
together with the invariant that the decoder has <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>1188</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1188</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">1188</span></span></span></span> parameters.</li>
<li><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">f</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">t</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">u</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{fixture}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6944em"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathrm">fixture</span></span></span></span></span>: a canonical record of SHA-256 digests of the exact corpus
bytes and exact split-manifest bytes. Even a byte change that leaves parsed
JSON meaning unchanged creates a different input identity.</li>
<li><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">u</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">_</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">v</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{source\_revision}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.9779em;vertical-align:-0.31em"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathrm">source_revision</span></span></span></span></span>: a verified source identity combining a baseline
revision with the exact forty course-owned scalar-reference source files.</li>
</ul>
<p>Here <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∥</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Vert</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:1em;vertical-align:-0.25em"></span><span class="mord">∥</span></span></span></span> means composition into the shared identity format’s named,
canonical fields, not writing three unframed strings beside one another.
That distinction matters: without field boundaries, different input sequences
can have the same concatenated bytes. The helper orders fields, serializes one
unambiguous record and hashes its complete bytes.</p>
<p>The settings fix eight BPE merges; decoder width, feed-forward width and context
capacity of four; one attention head and one block; stride one; training and
evaluation batch sizes of sixteen and one hundred twenty-eight; thirty-two
updates; learning rate <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.04</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.04</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">0.04</span></span></span></span>; gradient-norm cap <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">1</span></span></span></span>; training seed <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>39</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">39</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">39</span></span></span></span>;
generation seed <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>38</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">38</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">38</span></span></span></span>; bigram smoothing <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">1</span></span></span></span>; generation temperature <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.8</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">0.8</span></span></span></span>;
top-k four; and three generated tokens. The identity records floating-point
settings by their exact bit patterns rather than rounded display text.</p>

<p>The example verifies its compiled reference-source evidence first. It then
rejects changed corpus or split bytes before training or checkpoint work.
Only accepted fixed inputs reach the existing pipeline. The wrapper calls that
pipeline once; the pipeline itself performs primary training and replay.</p>

<h3 id="what-matching-identities-do-not-prove">What matching identities do not prove</h3>
<p>A matching digest identifies the same canonical input record, subject to the
hash’s collision-resistance assumption. It does not prove that the algorithm
is correct or that a new machine will reproduce every floating-point bit.</p>
<p>The source identity deliberately covers the forty scalar-reference source
files, not this chapter’s reporting wrapper or interface. Toolchain, locked
dependencies and arithmetic environment are recorded separately. A matching
source digest is therefore not evidence that two execution environments match.
The temporary checkpoint path is also outside the input identity; changing
that path does not change the model’s fixed inputs.</p>
<p>Likewise, exact checkpoint reload is narrower than complete job resumption.
This check does not restore every data cursor, in-flight operation or whole-job
continuation state. No laptop throughput is measured here.</p>

<h2 id="history-reporting-conditions-and-measuring-variation">History: reporting conditions and measuring variation</h2>
<p>A language-model score without its input conditions and scope does not identify
what was evaluated or establish which capabilities were checked.</p>
<p><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.03993v2">Model Cards for Model Reporting</a> was
presented in 2019. Mitchell and colleagues propose model documentation that
includes intended uses and evaluation conditions; a model card is not itself
proof of quality.</p>
<p>Model Cards describe evaluation conditions and intended uses; later fine-tuning
experiments study variation across initializations and data orders. Reporting
scope and measuring variation answer different questions.</p>
<p>In <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.06305v1">Fine-Tuning Pretrained Language Models: Weight Initializations, Data Orders, and Early Stopping</a>,
published in 2020, Dodge and colleagues study fine-tuning variability associated
with initialization and data order for pretrained language models. This does
not measure variability in the course’s tiny decoder.</p>
<p>Keep a fixed regression reference when changing an LLM pipeline, while recording
separately the evidence needed for quality, seed sensitivity and hardware claims.</p>
<p>The Rust reporting contrast uses the same observation. Reading only the mean
NLL with this expression gives a number:</p>
<pre class="astro-code github-dark-high-contrast" style="background-color:#0a0c10;color:#f0f3f6;overflow-x:auto" tabindex="0" data-language="rust" dir="ltr"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:#F0F3F6">trace</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#FF9492">    .</span><span style="color:#DBB7FF">observation</span><span style="color:#F0F3F6">()</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#FF9492">    .</span><span style="color:#DBB7FF">final_evaluation</span><span style="color:#F0F3F6">()</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#FF9492">    .</span><span style="color:#DBB7FF">decoder</span><span style="color:#F0F3F6">()</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#FF9492">    .</span><span style="color:#DBB7FF">mean_nll</span><span style="color:#F0F3F6">()</span></span></code></pre>
<p><code>trace.report()</code> also states the evaluation unit, input identity, replay
accounting and limits. It does not retrain a historical model or execute a seed
sweep.</p>

<p>Repeating seed <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>39</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">39</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">39</span></span></span></span> checks repeatability under fixed conditions. It does not
estimate variability across seeds. Those are complementary checks, not
interchangeable evidence.</p>

<h2 id="run-the-reference-without-changing-its-inputs">Run the reference without changing its inputs</h2>
<p>The example obtains verified source evidence and owns its temporary checkpoint
location. Its report comes directly from the checked scalar observation, not
from parsing a previous human-readable report.</p>

<h2 id="keep-the-three-evidence-layers-separate">Keep the three evidence layers separate</h2>
<p>The digest identifies the fixed inputs. The counts and generated token IDs
describe checked behavior on those inputs. The final card keeps future quality,
job-resumption and hardware claims outside the reference’s evidence boundary.</p>
<figure class="course-diagram reference-core-handoff-diagram" data-diagram-style="course-v1" data-visualization-id="reference-core-handoff" tabindex="0" aria-labelledby="reference-handoff-title" aria-describedby="reference-handoff-description"> <figcaption class="course-diagram__caption"> <h3 id="reference-handoff-title">A reference identity is not a capability certificate</h3> <p id="reference-handoff-description" class="course-diagram__description">The configuration, exact corpus and split bytes, and verified scalar-reference source determine the input identity. Separate checks observe replay, fixed-window evaluation, reload and cached generation. Neither the identity nor those checks establishes useful language quality, complete job resumption or laptop throughput.</p> </figcaption> <div class="course-diagram__grid"> <section class="course-diagram__card-stack" data-diagram-card data-diagram-box> <h4>Identify the fixed inputs</h4> <dl> <dt>SHA-256 identity of the fixed input record</dt> <dd class="course-diagram__technical"><code><bdi dir="ltr">cd06104ff61dc8a0c6cbe6e842847952343050eb4942c79aa1d17e8d0d0bb648</bdi></code></dd> <dt>Learned scalar parameters</dt><dd><code>1188</code></dd> </dl> </section> <section class="course-diagram__card-stack" data-diagram-card data-diagram-box> <h4>Read the checked reference behavior</h4> <dl> <dt>Overlapping test-window target slots</dt><dd><code>1744</code></dd> <dt>Within-document transition occurrences</dt><dd><code>442</code></dd> <dt>Generated token IDs</dt><dd><code><bdi dir="ltr">[260,34,34]</bdi></code></dd> </dl> </section> <section class="course-diagram__card-stack" data-diagram-card data-diagram-box> <h4>Keep unmeasured capabilities separate</h4><p class="course-diagram__description">Not established: useful language quality, complete job resumption or laptop throughput.</p> </section> </div> </figure>

<h2 id="optional-practice-inspect-the-boundary">Optional practice: inspect the boundary</h2>
<p>Run the example and inspect its report:</p>
<pre class="astro-code github-dark-high-contrast" style="background-color:#0a0c10;color:#f0f3f6;overflow-x:auto" tabindex="0" data-language="sh" dir="ltr"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:#FFB757">cargo</span><span style="color:#ADDCFF"> run</span><span style="color:#91CBFF"> --quiet</span><span style="color:#91CBFF"> --locked</span><span style="color:#91CBFF"> -p</span><span style="color:#ADDCFF"> ch40-reference-core-handoff</span></span></code></pre>
<ol>
<li>Find the identity, target-count basis and metric unit in the output. Explain
why a digest alone would not replace the replay and reload checks.</li>
<li>Run the demo’s tests. Identify the tests that change configuration, corpus,
split bytes and source identity without training. Explain why constructing
an identity for changed inputs does not admit them to the fixed reference run.</li>
<li>Explain why a successful checkpoint round trip cannot justify the statement
“the complete training job can resume,” and why <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>1744</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1744</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">1744</span></span></span></span> must not be labeled
“distinct test transitions.”</li>
</ol>
<details><summary>Answers: input identity, evidence scope and repeated target slots</summary><ol>
<li>The digest binds inputs; replay and reload compare actual behavior. Neither
kind of evidence substitutes for the other. The target-count basis explicitly
derives <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>2048</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2048</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">2048</span></span></span></span> targets per schedule and <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>4096</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4096</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">4096</span></span></span></span> for primary plus replay.
The reported mean NLL uses nats per overlapping window-target slot.</li>
<li>The pure mutation tests construct different identities without calling the
pipeline. The runner separately requires the exact accepted corpus and split
bytes, so an identity is not an admission permit.</li>
<li>The checkpoint check covers persisted model, optimizer and tokenizer state
plus a fixed logit probe, not every whole-job continuation dependency. The
<span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>1744</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1744</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">1744</span></span></span></span> denominator counts overlapping window-target slots; the underlying
documents contain <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>442</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">442</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">442</span></span></span></span> transition occurrences.</li>
</ol></details>

<h2 id="what-the-next-extension-must-preserve">What the next extension must preserve</h2>
<p>You now have an identified scalar reference and a precisely bounded report.
A later change can be compared with that reference, while carrying its own
input identity and evidence. Chapter 41 will address governed corpus acquisition.
New data, larger models, accelerator execution, quality evaluation and complete
job resumption each require their own checks; none is already established by

CPU reference decoder in Rust through validation-selected training, a fixed-fixture comparison over overlapping window-target slots, exact reload, and KV-cached generation. Distinguish that comparison from the unreported policy that would score 442 within-document transitions once each with the longest causal prefix capped at four tokens and only its newest-position distribution; numeric NLL and PPL are not reported for that policy. This integration example does not establish useful language quality or laptop-scale performance.</p> <aside class="lesson-objective"> <strong>In this chapter</strong> <p>Run one deterministic scalar reference decoder end to end on bilingual data, report mean NLL and perplexity for its overlapping test-window slots, distinguish those 1,744 slots from 442 within-document transition occurrences, and data-cheat-sheet-page="1" role="group" aria-label="Terms 1–10 of 17; page 1 of 2" data-astro-cid-ws375rge> <dl class="cheat-sheet-terms" data-astro-cid-ws375rge> <div class="cheat-sheet-term" data-astro-cid-ws375rge> <dt data-astro-cid-ws375rge>Autoregressive factorization</dt> <dd data-astro-cid-ws375rge>The causal decomposition of joint sequence probability into one next-token conditional factor per position, with each factor depending only on the earlier prefix.</dd> </div><div class="cheat-sheet-term" data-astro-cid-ws375rge> <dt data-astro-cid-ws375rge>Bitwise training replay</dt> <dd data-astro-cid-ws375rge>A repeat of the frozen training run with identical data, initialization, batch order, and arithmetic environment that reproduces every recorded training event and gradient diagnostic, the selected checkpoint, every final model value, and the final optimizer state bit for bit.</dd> </div><div class="cheat-sheet-term" data-astro-cid-ws375rge> <dt data-astro-cid-ws375rge>Decoder-only LLM</dt> <dd data-astro-cid-ws375rge>An autoregressive language model with a causal decoder stack and no separate encoder, mapping a bounded earlier-token context to next-token logits.</dd> </div><div class="cheat-sheet-term" data-astro-cid-ws375rge> <dt data-astro-cid-ws375rge>End-to-end LLM pipeline</dt> <dd data-astro-cid-ws375rge>The course path that turns frozen documents into BPE tokens and causal batches, trains and selects a decoder before one local fixed-fixture evaluation, restores it, and generates text.</dd> </div><div class="cheat-sheet-term" data-astro-cid-ws375rge> <dt data-astro-cid-ws375rge>Exact checkpoint round trip</dt> <dd data-astro-cid-ws375rge>Saving and loading the selected state so checkpoint bytes, model and optimizer bits, BPE ranks, selected step, and RNG state all reproduce exactly.</dd> </div><div class="cheat-sheet-term" data-astro-cid-ws375rge> <dt data-astro-cid-ws375rge>Exact logit probe</dt> <dd data-astro-cid-ws375rge>A deliberately narrow check that the restored decoder reproduces every logit bit for the fixed At input, without claiming that every possible input was compared.</dd> </div><div class="cheat-sheet-term" data-astro-cid-ws375rge> <dt data-astro-cid-ws375rge>Fixed-fixture regression evidence</dt> <dd data-astro-cid-ws375rge>A known result rerun to detect changes in checked behavior; later executions retain the lower decoder window-slot mean NLL as a regression condition, so the gap is neither an independent estimate of generalization nor evidence of architecture superiority.</dd> </div><div class="cheat-sheet-term" data-astro-cid-ws375rge> <dt data-astro-cid-ws375rge>Frozen alpha-one bigram baseline</dt> <dd data-astro-cid-ws375rge>An add-one-smoothed, one-token-context model fitted only on training tokens and frozen before it scores the final ordered test slots.</dd> </div><div class="cheat-sheet-term" data-astro-cid-ws375rge> <dt data-astro-cid-ws375rge>Frozen document split</dt> <dd data-astro-cid-ws375rge>A fixed assignment of whole documents to training, validation, and test roles, preventing test-reserved text from influencing tokenizer learning, parameter updates, or selection.</dd> </div><div class="cheat-sheet-term" data-astro-cid-ws375rge> <dt data-astro-cid-ws375rge>Joint sequence probability</dt> <dd data-astro-cid-ws375rge>The probability assigned to an entire token sequence, computed as the product of the observed next-token conditional probability at every position.</dd> </div> </dl> </div><div class="cheat-sheet-page" data-cheat-sheet-page="2" role="group" aria-label="Terms 11–17 of 17; page 2 of 2" hidden data-astro-cid-ws375rge> <dl class="cheat-sheet-terms" data-astro-cid-ws375rge> <div class="cheat-sheet-term" data-astro-cid-ws375rge> <dt data-astro-cid-ws375rge>KV-cached generation</dt> <dd data-astro-cid-ws375rge>In this fixture, generation after prompt prefill retains per-block key/value state and decodes only tokens needed for later logits, while matching the complete-prefix reference’s draws, token decisions, stopping, and final RNG state.</dd> </div><div <h2 id="predict-the-boundary-before-predicting-the-output">Predict the boundary before predicting the output</h2>
<p>The corpus contains <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">8</span></span></span></span> training documents, <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">2</span></span></span></span> validation documents, and <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">2</span></span></span></span>
test documents. The first prediction is about information flow: only the
training documents may teach BPE merge ranks, update decoder parameters, or fit
the count baseline. Validation may choose a trained state. Test evidence may do
neither.</p>
<p>Eight training-only BPE merges produce vocabulary size <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>266</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">266</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">266</span></span></span></span>. context capacity <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C=4</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6833em"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0715em">C</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">4</span></span></span></span> and stride one, the encoded partitions produce <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>1820</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1820</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">1820</span></span></span></span>,

<p>Before reading the result, predict:</p>
<ol>
<li>whether two runs from training seed <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>39</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">39</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">39</span></span></span></span> select the same state bit for bit;</li>
<li>whether test loss is visible before that state is fixed;</li>

probe; and</li>

would present the decoder with the maximal available prefix of at most four
immediately preceding tokens and use only the distribution at the newest
position. Chapter 39 does not report that metric’s mean NLL or perplexity, so
the <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>1744</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1744</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">1744</span></span></span></span>-slot values must not be read as corpus scores over <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>442</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">442</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">442</span></span></span></span> transitions.</p>
<p>The lower decoder slot mean-NLL ordering is retained across later executions, so it is useful
regression evidence. It is not an untouched independent estimate of
generalization or evidence of architecture-wide decoder superiority.</p>

<h2 id="from-short-count-contexts-to-autoregressive-transformer-llms">From short count contexts to autoregressive Transformer LLMs</h2>
<p>A count-based bigram estimates the next token from one preceding token and cannot share statistical strength through learned features or use the longer causal prefix.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.jmlr.org/papers/volume3/bengio03a/bengio03a.pdf">A Neural Probabilistic Language Model</a>
supports this bounded claim: Bengio and colleagues describe traditional n-gram generalization through short overlapping sequences and show a neural probability function that learns distributed word representations and benefits from longer contexts; their model is not a Transformer or this course pipeline.</p>
<p><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.02629">Generalization in Adaptive Data Analysis and Holdout Reuse</a>
supplies the evidence warning. Dwork and colleagues show that adaptive repeated
reuse of a standard holdout can overfit that holdout; this general warning does
not establish any fact about the capstone fixture, its score, or its local access
count.</p>
<p><a href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/1706.03762">Attention Is All You Need</a> supports a later
boundary: Vaswani and colleagues define the Transformer and mask decoder self-attention so a position cannot read later positions; their published architecture is an encoder-decoder model and does not define this course data, checkpoint, or generation policy.</p>
<p><a href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2005.14165">Language Models are Few-Shot Learners</a>
supplies the scaled-LLM context: Brown and colleagues train GPT-3, a
175-billion-parameter autoregressive Transformer language model based on the
GPT-2 architecture, and evaluate zero-, one-, and few-shot tasks without gradient
updates or fine-tuning; none of its scale or capability results transfers to
this tiny teaching run.</p>
<p>Neural language models learned distributed token features and longer-context probability functions; the Transformer supplied masked self-attention, and later autoregressive Transformer language models scaled that training objective.</p>
<p>This course capstone combines training-only tokenizer learning, causal
next-token updates, validation-selected state, within-execution selection
isolation, fixed-fixture regression evaluation, exact checkpoint round-trip, and
stateful generation; these are local evidence rules, not requirements of the
cited papers.</p>
<p>Compare the training-only alpha-one bigram with the validation-selected causal
decoder on the same ordered overlapping window-target slots. Four tokens is the
decoder’s context capacity; the four slot positions expose one through four
in-window context tokens. The mean-NLL gap retained by later executions is fixed-fixture
regression evidence, not causal attribution to context or attention and not an
independent generalization estimate. Bengio and colleagues’ discussion of
overlapping sequences does not define this course’s stride-one slot weighting.</p>
<p>Count n-grams provided a strong short-context baseline; learned distributed
features and masked self-attention made longer learned computation possible, and
scaled autoregressive Transformers became one major family of modern LLMs. This
capstone demonstrates local end-to-end responsibility boundaries at inspectable
scale while treating the known lower decoder window-slot mean NLL only as a regression
condition for this fixed fixture.</p>
<p>The executable contrast is narrow: a one-token count context and a decoder with
four-token context capacity score the same <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>1744</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1744</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">1744</span></span></span></span> repeated window slots on this
frozen corpus. The lower slot mean NLL verifies the retained fixed-fixture
ordering. The separate policy would score the <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>442</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">442</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">442</span></span></span></span> transition occurrences once
each with the longest causal prefix capped at four tokens and only its newest-position
distribution, but its numeric mean NLL and PPL are not reported. The ordering is
also not an untouched independent estimate of generalization, a universal
architecture ranking, or evidence of useful generation quality.</p>

<h2 id="assemble-apis-instead-of-copying-algorithms">Assemble APIs instead of copying algorithms</h2>
<p><code>run_capstone</code> starts by parsing the checked corpus and split. It
learns BPE from the training partition, encodes each document without joining
boundaries, fits the alpha-one bigram from the same training tokens, and builds
separate causal epochs for training updates and validation. It does not build
the test epoch at this stage.</p>
<p>Two decoder runs receive the same initialization and batch-order seed. Each
executes all <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>32</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">32</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">32</span></span></span></span> updates. The implementation compares every training event,
loss checkpoint, optimizer moment, selected step, and model value by bit pattern.
Only after replay agrees and validation fixes the selection does the run prepare
final evaluation. <code>TrainingResult</code> owns both the retained selected state and an
independent decoder with the same values. <code>SelectedDecoder</code> borrows both. The run
then materializes the test epoch, records two facts—<span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>436</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">436</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">436</span></span></span></span> windows
and <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">4</span></span></span></span> mini-batches—and moves the epoch into <code>FinalEvaluator</code>. The evaluator
owns the epoch and the local permission to evaluate it once. Immediately before
opening that local test gate, it verifies that the decoder’s configuration,
ordered names and shapes, and every parameter bit still match the retained
state; this prevents a changed decoder from being evaluated under stale
selection metadata without making another model copy. The evaluator then scores
the borrowed model and consumes its permission. It compares both models on the
same ordered <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>1744</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1744</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">1744</span></span></span></span> overlapping window-target slots, including the same repeated
transition occurrences. The decoder has context capacity four, but its slot
predictions use actual in-window context lengths <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">1</span></span></span></span>, <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">2</span></span></span></span>, <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">3</span></span></span></span>, and <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">4</span></span></span></span>. The
separate policy would score all <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>442</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">442</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">442</span></span></span></span> occurrences once each, use the longest
available causal prefix capped at four tokens and only its newest-position distribution,
and report no numeric mean NLL or PPL.</p>
<p>The permission, not either borrowed object, is the one-use resource. This is an
executable boundary inside this run, not a claim that the repository globally
prevents other code from reading the corpus. Later report assembly retains the
derived counts and metric evidence, not a cloned epoch.</p>
<p>The pipeline retains the lower decoder window-slot mean NLL as an explicitly named
fixed-fixture regression condition; <code>FinalEvaluator</code> itself remains neutral to
which model is lower. The learner evidence uses
<code>decoder_lower_on_fixture:true</code> and records
<code>scope:fixed-fixture-regression</code>, <code>within_run_selection_isolated:true</code>,
<code>independent_generalization_estimate:false</code>, and
<code>architecture_superiority_evidence:false</code>.</p>
<p>The report derives the displayed count of <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>1188</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1188</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">1188</span></span></span></span> learned scalars by calling
<code>primary.selected_state().scalar_count()</code>. That method computes the count by
summing the lengths of the parameter tensors in the retained graph-free state
selected by validation; it neither reads a stored count nor initializes another
decoder.</p>
<p>Final evaluation and durable checkpoint storage have different ownership needs.
Evaluation only borrows the retained selected state and matching decoder. After
evaluation, the checkpoint must coexist with the complete training result, so
<code>Checkpoint::from_snapshot</code> deliberately copies the selected graph-free state
and optimizer persistence state. That copy is required because the training
result and checkpoint must remain independently usable.</p>
<p>Re-encoding the loaded checkpoint must reproduce the saved bytes, and its model
and optimizer bits, BPE ranks, step, and RNG state must all agree. Before
consuming the checkpoint, the pipeline records the tokenizer, selected step,
optimizer state, and saved RNG value needed by later evidence. It then calls
<code>loaded.into_model()</code>, which moves the owned model buffers into a decoder. The
separate <code>At</code> probe compares that decoder with
<code>primary.selected_model()</code> and must match bit for bit. Only then does the loaded
model run cached and complete-prefix generation from prompt <code>A</code> and
the saved RNG state. <code>generation_evidence</code> encodes the prompt once into one
<code>prompt_ids</code> vector. Both generation paths temporarily read that vector through
immutable references. After both calls finish and the local vector is no longer
needed for calculation, <code>GenerationEvidence</code> takes ownership of the same vector;
moving the <code>Vec</code> transfers its existing buffer instead of cloning the prompt IDs
for the report.</p>

<p>The runnable evidence requires every final claim together. It rejects a changed
test ordering, a changed lower-decoder slot-metric regression condition, a
replay with different bits, altered checkpoint state or probe logits, or any
cached sampling divergence. That requirement protects known fixture behavior; it
does not promote the ordering into independent generalization evidence.</p>

<h2 id="follow-the-one-way-pipeline">Follow the one-way pipeline</h2>
<p>The figure begins with fixed document roles and training-only tokenizer learning.
It then follows causal windows into the decoder and places the validation-selected
state before a double-marked local test gate. Test loss has no path back to an
update or selection in this run. The test card identifies the <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>1744</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1744</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">1744</span></span></span></span> observations
as overlapping window-target slots and labels the values as mean NLL in nats per
slot. The separate policy would score all <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>442</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">442</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">442</span></span></span></span> within-document transition
occurrences once each, use the longest causal prefix capped at four tokens and only its
newest-position distribution, and report no numeric mean NLL or PPL. The known
ordering remains a fixed-fixture regression condition, not independent
generalization evidence.</p>
