# Chapter 40 canonical-English commitments

This is author evidence, not a language review or publication verdict.

## Evidence boundary

The unchanged scalar pipeline is the executable source of all model behavior.
The demo owns Chapter40-specific orchestration and reporting. The accepted
reference source manifest binds forty course-owned scalar-reference source files.
It intentionally does not bind workspace dependency membership, the demo or UI.
Actual locked dependencies/toolchain/arithmetic environment remain separately
recorded execution evidence. No digest promises cross-environment bit identity.

Run02 actual demo tests: four passing cases and one successful binary execution.
Actual stdout is publish/rust/demos/ch40-reference-core-handoff/expected.txt:
1904 bytes, SHA-256 f2e07dd9b69369fe928e6c7577cdf8ae67d82f620f0887d6ddcc4d7608b9fe90.
The reference identity is
cd06104ff61dc8a0c6cbe6e842847952343050eb4942c79aa1d17e8d0d0bb648.

## Commitments and surface ownership

C01 — Complete lesson/objective/description and course card: identify the problem
as preserving a fixed scalar comparison point before extension, not building a
new model or demonstrating laptop-scale capability. Begin with explanation,
not learner prediction. The chapter and metadata must agree on this outcome.

C02 — Formula section/symbol inventory/Rust identity excerpt: bind configuration,
fixture and verified source identity as named canonical records. Explain each
input locally and composition versus unframed concatenation. SHA-256 is mature
supporting-library plumbing, not a hand-written taught implementation. State
256 bits/64 lower-case hex characters as representation, not confidence.

C03 — Configuration/worked input: eight training documents, two validation
and two test documents, eighteen settings and the1188parameter invariant.
Source-only identity is not dependency/environment equivalence. Temporary path
and report/UI are outside its comparison boundary. Changed corpus/split bytes
refuse before pipeline execution; pure identity construction is not admission.

C04 — Worked example/training report: primary and replay are independent repeats
of the same fixed schedule in one invocation, each32 updates times16 windows
times4 valid targets=2048, aggregate4096. Counts are schedule-derived, not new
instrumentation. Evaluation and generation remain separate. Replay does not
measure seed variation; bitwise claims stay within actual validated execution.
Here independent means separately executed from the same seed39, not
statistically independent seed samples. The lesson and sheet state this
distinction explicitly while preserving the literal report field name.

C05 — Evaluation/figure/sheet/answers:1744 overlapping window-target slots,
442 within-document transition occurrences. Decoder/bigram mean NLL values
3.8660875470071363 and3.9813427143837696 nats/slot, displayed approximately to9
decimals. Same slots include repetitions. Known ordering is fixed-fixture
regression, not independent generalization or architecture-superiority evidence.
Once-per-transition policy uses longest available causal prefix <=4 and newest
position only; numeric NLL/PPL are not reported.

C06 — Checkpoint/report/answers/sheet: encoded bytes, model/optimizer bits and
tokenizer round trip; fixed At probe [67,118] logits bitwise. No complete job
resumption claim, all-input correctness claim or emergency recovery claim.

C07 — Generation/report/figure/sheet: prompt A, IDs[260,34,34], Cyrillic т plus

fn safe_identifier(s: &str) -> bool {
    let reserved = [
        "self", "super", "crate", "mod", "pub", "fn", "type", "struct", "enum", "use", "impl",
        "where", "const", "static", "async", "await", "move", "match", "loop", "if", "else", "for",
        "while", "let", "ref", "return", "true", "false", "trait", "as", "in", "extern", "unsafe",
        "dyn",
    ];
    !s.is_empty()
        && !reserved.contains(&s)
        && (s.as_bytes()[0].is_ascii_lowercase() || s.starts_with('_'))
        && s.bytes()
            .all(|b| b.is_ascii_lowercase() || b.is_ascii_digit() || b == b'_')
}

pub fn parse_fragment(filename: &str, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<(String, String)>, String> {
    if bytes.len() > 65_536
        || !bytes.is_ascii()
        || !bytes.ends_with(b"\n")
        || bytes.ends_with(b"\n\n")
        || bytes.contains(&b'\r')
    {
        return Err("fragment must be bounded ASCII/LF with exactly one final LF".into());
    }
    let text = std::str::from_utf8(bytes).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let mut records = Vec::new();
    for record in text[..text.len() - 1].split("\n\n") {
        let lines: Vec<_> = record.split('\n').collect();
        if lines.len() != 3 || lines[0] != "version=1" {
            return Err("exactly3 version/module/source lines required".into());
        }
        let module = lines[1].strip_prefix("module=").ok_or("missing module")?;
        let source = lines[2].strip_prefix("source=").ok_or("missing source")?;
        let stem = source
            .strip_prefix("src/")
            .and_then(|s| s.strip_suffix(".rs"))
            .ok_or("unsafe source")?;
        if !stem.split('/').all(safe_identifier) || source.contains('\\') {
            return Err("unsafe Rust source".into());
        }
        let normalized = format!("functional::{}", stem.replace('/', "::"));
        if module != normalized || !FUNCTIONAL_OWNERS.contains(&(filename, source)) {
            return Err("module/path/owner mismatch".into());
        }
        records.push((module.to_owned(), source.to_owned()));
    }
    if records.windows(2).any(|x| x[0].0 >= x[1].0) {
        return Err("records must have unique sorted module order".into());
    }
    Ok(records)
}

fn regular_path(root: &Path, relative: &str) -> Result<PathBuf, String> {
    let mut path = root.to_path_buf();
    for component in relative.split('/') {
        if component.is_empty() || component == "." || component == ".." {
            return Err("unsafe path".into());
        }
        path.push(component);
        let meta = fs::symlink_metadata(&path).map_err(|e| format!("{}: {e}", path.display()))?;
        if meta.file_type().is_symlink() {
            return Err(format!("symlink rejected: {}", path.display()));
        }
    }
    if !path.is_file() {
        return Err(format!("nonregular file: {}", path.display()));
    }
    Ok(path)
}

#[derive(Default)]
struct Tree {
    children: BTreeMap<String, Tree>,
    source: Option<String>,
}
impl Tree {
    fn insert(&mut self, module: &str, source: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
        let mut cursor = self;
        for name in module.split("::").skip(1) {
            if cursor.source.is_some() {
                return Err("module-prefix collision".into());
            }
            cursor = cursor.children.entry(name.to_owned()).or_default();
        }
        if cursor.source.is_some() || !cursor.children.is_empty() {
            return Err("duplicate/prefix-colliding module".into());
        }
        cursor.source = Some(source.to_owned());
        Ok(())
    }
    fn render(&self) -> String {
        self.children.iter().map(|(name,node)|{
            if let Some(source)=&node.source {
                format!("pub mod {name} {{ include!(concat!(env!(\"CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR\"), \"/{source}\")); }}\n")
            } else { format!("pub mod {name} {{\n{}}}\n",node.render()) }
        }).collect()
    }
}

pub fn registry_source(crate_root: &Path) -> Result<String, String> {
    let directory = crate_root.join("module-registry/functional-v1");
    let mut names = Vec::new();
    if directory.exists() {
        for part in ["module-registry", "module-registry/functional-v1"] {
            let m = fs::symlink_metadata(crate_root.join(part)).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
            if !m.is_dir() || m.file_type().is_symlink() {
                return Err("unsafe registry directory".into());
            }
        }
        for entry in fs::read_dir(&directory).map_err(|e| e.to_string())? {
            let entry = entry.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
            let name = entry
                .file_name()
                .into_string()
                .map_err(|_| "nonUTF8 filename")?;
            if !FUNCTIONAL_OWNERS.iter().any(|(f, _)| *f == name) {
                return Err(format!("unknown fragment {name}"));
            }
            names.push(name);
        }
    }
    names.sort();
    let mut sources = BTreeSet::new();
    let mut tree = Tree::default();
    for name in names {
        let path = regular_path(crate_root, &format!("module-registry/functional-v1/{name}"))?;
        let bytes = fs::read(path).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        let records = parse_fragment(&name, &bytes)?;
        let required: BTreeSet<_> = FUNCTIONAL_OWNERS
            .iter()
            .filter(|(f, _)| *f == name)
            .map(|(_, p)| *p)
            .collect();
        if records
            .iter()
            .map(|(_, s)| s.as_str())
            .collect::<BTreeSet<_>>()
            != required
        {
            return Err("fragment omits an owned source".into());
        }
        for (module, source) in records {
            regular_path(crate_root, &source)?;
            if !sources.insert(source.clone()) {
                return Err("duplicate source".into());
            }
            tree.insert(&module, &source)?;
        }
    }
    for (_, source) in FUNCTIONAL_OWNERS {
        if crate_root.join(source).exists() && !sources.contains(*source) {
            return Err(format!("unregistered source {source}"));
        }
    }
    Ok(format!(
        "pub mod reference_source_identity {{ include!(concat!(env!(\"CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR\"), \"/src/reference_source_identity.rs\")); }}\npub mod functional {{\n{}}}\n",
        tree.render()
    ))
}

fn main() {
    let crate_root =
        PathBuf::from(std::env::var_os("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR").expect("Cargo manifest directory"));
    let repository = crate_root
        .parent()
        .and_then(Path::parent)
        .and_then(Path::parent)
        .expect("repository root");
    let out = PathBuf::from(std::env::var_os("OUT_DIR").expect("Cargo output directory"));
    let manifest = "configs/functional-reference-source-v1.json";
    regular_path(repository, manifest).expect("safe approved manifest");
    println!(
        "cargo:rerun-if-changed={}",
        repository.join(manifest).display()
    );
    let mut census = format!(
        "const COMPILED_MANIFEST: &[u8] = include_bytes!(concat!(env!(\"CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR\"), \"/../../../{manifest}\"));\nconst COMPILED_FILES: &[(&str, &[u8])] = &[\n"
    );
    for path in SOURCE_CENSUS {
        regular_path(repository, path).expect("safe census path");
        println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed={}", repository.join(path).display());
        census.push_str(&format!("({path:?}, include_bytes!(concat!(env!(\"CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR\"), \"/../../../{path}\"))),\n"));
    }
    census.push_str("];\n");
    fs::write(out.join("reference-source-census.rs"), census).expect("write compile-time census");
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed=module-registry/functional-v1");
    for (_, path) in FUNCTIONAL_OWNERS {
        println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed={path}");
    }
    let registry = registry_source(&crate_root).expect("closed functional module registry");
    fs::write(out.join("functional-modules.rs"), registry).expect("write owned module registry");
}

reading.roleRequirement: Explain the need for a fixed comparison point when extending an existing tokenizer/decoder pipeline. State the limitation of unidentified changing inputs before naming identity machinery; do not ask the learner a question or request a prediction.
reading.value: The problem: changes need a fixed comparison point The previous chapter joined the tokenizer, decoder, training, evaluation, checkpoint and generation code. Now the course will extend that system. If the data, configuration and code change together, a changed result no longer tells you which version you observed. You need a fixed reference that identifies its inputs and states exactly what its checks establish. This chapter keeps the small scalar decoder unchanged. It gives that reference an input identity and a report whose claims stay attached to their evidence. The identity identifies the fixed inputs. The checks establish which behavior this execution reproduced. Neither establishes useful laptop-scale capability.

reading.roleRequirement: Interpret actual fixed reference observations with local counts,units and scopes. Distinguish each2048-target schedule from4096 aggregate and1744 overlapping target slots from442 underlying transition occurrences. Scope replay,reload and generated tokens to the validated reference,not new capabilities.
reading.value: What the reference actually does The fixture assigns 8 documents to training, 2 to validation and 2 to test. The decoder has 1188 learned scalar parameters and context capacity 4 tokens. Its primary training schedule and separately executed replay each perform 32 updates on full batches of 16 windows, with 4 valid targets per window. Therefore, each schedule consumes 32\cdot16\cdot4=2048 valid training targets. One pipeline invocation includes both schedules: 4096 targets altogether. These counts are derived from the frozen full-batch schedule, not from a new runtime token counter. Evaluation targets and generated tokens are separate quantities. The report’s independent_schedules field counts two separately executed copies of the same schedule from training seed 39, not statistically independent seed samples. The replay agrees bit for bit with the primary training result in this execution. The selected decoder and frozen bigram then score the same 1744 overlapping test-window target slots. Their mean negative log-likelihoods are approximately 3.866087547 and 3.981342714 nats per slot, respectively. This known comparison is a regression check: rerunning it can expose changes in the checked behavior. It is not an independent estimate of generalization. There are only 442 within-document transition occurrences in those test documents. Overlapping windows repeat occurrences, so 1744 is not a count of distinct transitions. A separate policy would score each occurrence once, using the longest available causal prefix capped at four tokens and only its newest-position distribution. This run does not report numeric mean NLL or perplexity under that policy. The checkpoint round trip preserves its encoded bytes, model and optimizer bits, and tokenizer. The restored decoder reproduces logits for the fixed At probe, encoded as token IDs [67,118]. Cached and complete-prefix generation agree on token IDs [260,34,34]: Cyrillic т followed by two spaces. Agreement checks the two generation paths; those three tokens do not demonstrate useful language quality.

reading.roleRequirement: Introduce the reference input-identity equation in the solution's reading order. The immediately following symbol/settings unit explains its inputs and canonical encoding; this introductory equation unit need not duplicate that explanation.
reading.value: The solution: identify inputs, then interpret evidence R_{\mathrm{ref}}=\operatorname{SHA256}(\mathrm{config}_{1188}\Vert\mathrm{fixture}\Vert\mathrm{source\_revision})

reading.roleRequirement: Define each formula symbol and fixed setting where needed,including the verified forty-source-file boundary and separate execution-environment evidence. Explain why fixture changes refuse before training and why a pure constructed identity is not admission.
reading.value: The identity’s symbols and fixed settings R_{\mathrm{ref}} is a 256-bit digest, displayed as 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. Its three named inputs are: \mathrm{config}_{1188}: a canonical record of eighteen tiny-run settings, together with the invariant that the decoder has 1188 parameters. \mathrm{fixture}: a canonical record of SHA-256 digests of the exact corpus bytes and exact split-manifest bytes. Even a byte change that leaves parsed JSON meaning unchanged creates a different input identity. \mathrm{source\_revision}: a verified source identity combining a baseline revision with the exact forty course-owned scalar-reference source files. Here \Vert means composition into the shared identity format’s named, canonical fields, not writing three unframed strings beside one another. That distinction matters: without field boundaries, different input sequences can have the same concatenated bytes. The helper orders fields, serializes one unambiguous record and hashes its complete bytes. The settings fix eight BPE merges; decoder width, feed-forward width and context capacity of four; one attention head and one block; stride one; training and evaluation batch sizes of sixteen and one hundred twenty-eight; thirty-two updates; learning rate 0.04; gradient-norm cap 1; training seed 39; generation seed 38; bigram smoothing 1; generation temperature 0.8; top-k four; and three generated tokens. The identity records floating-point settings by their exact bit patterns rather than rounded display text. Bind configuration, exact fixture bytes and verified scalar-reference source to one input identity. rust/demos/ch40-reference-core-handoff/src/lib.rs#reference-input-identity /// Bind every tiny-config field, including exact represented floating values. /// The count is the reference decoder's required 1,188-parameter invariant. pub fn tiny_config_identity() -> Result<ArtifactIdentity, IdentityError> { let config = CapstoneConfig::tiny(); let fields = [ ("parameters", "1188".to_owned()), ("bpe_merges", config.bpe_merges().to_string()), ("model_width", config.model_width().to_string()), ("heads", config.heads().to_string()), ( "feed_forward_width", config.feed_forward_width().to_string(), ), ("layers", config.layers().to_string()), ("context_length", config.context_length().to_string()), ("window_stride", config.window_stride().to_string()), ("update_batch_size", config.update_batch_size().to_string()), ( "evaluation_batch_size", config.evaluation_batch_size().to_string(), ), ("updates", config.updates().to_string()), ( "learning_rate_f64_bits", format!("{:016x}", config.learning_rate().to_bits()), ), ( "max_gradient_norm_f64_bits", format!("{:016x}", config.max_gradient_norm().to_bits()), ), ("seed", config.seed().to_string()), ("generation_seed", config.generation_seed().to_string()), ( "bigram_alpha_f64_bits", format!("{:016x}", config.bigram_alpha().to_bits()), ), ( "generation_temperature_f64_bits", format!("{:016x}", config.generation_temperature().to_bits()), ), ("generation_top_k", config.generation_top_k().to_string()), ("generation_tokens", config.generation_tokens().to_string()), ]; ArtifactIdentity::new( "scalar_reference_config", fields.iter().map(|(key, value)| (*key, value.as_str())), ) } /// Pure identity construction, also usable by mutation tests without training. /// An identity by itself does not admit alternate inputs to the reference run. pub fn reference_input_identity( config: &ArtifactIdentity, corpus: &[u8], splits: &[u8], source: &ArtifactIdentity, ) -> Result<ArtifactIdentity, IdentityError> { let corpus_digest = sha256(corpus); let splits_digest = sha256(splits); let fixture = ArtifactIdentity::new( "scalar_reference_fixture", [ ("corpus_sha256", corpus_digest.as_hex()), ("splits_sha256", splits_digest.as_hex()), ], )?; let config_bytes = canonical_string(config)?; let fixture_bytes = canonical_string(&fixture)?; let source_bytes = canonical_string(source)?; ArtifactIdentity::new( "scalar_reference_run", [ ("config_1188", config_bytes.as_str()), ("fixture", fixture_bytes.as_str()), ("source_revision", source_bytes.as_str()), ], ) } The example verifies its compiled reference-source evidence first. It then rejects changed corpus or split bytes before training or checkpoint work. Only accepted fixed inputs reach the existing pipeline. The wrapper calls that pipeline once; the pipeline itself performs primary training and replay. Reject changed fixtures, run the unchanged scalar pipeline and retain only its checked observation. rust/demos/ch40-reference-core-handoff/src/lib.rs#reference-handoff /// Refuse changed fixtures before model/checkpoint work, then call the existing /// capstone once. That call already includes primary training and full replay. pub fn run_reference_handoff( corpus_source: &str, split_source: &str, checkpoint_path: impl AsRef<Path>, source: &ReferenceSourceProof, ) -> Result<ReferenceHandoffTrace, ReferenceHandoffError> { if sha256(corpus_source.as_bytes()).as_hex() != CORPUS_SHA256 { return Err(ReferenceHandoffError::FixtureMismatch("corpus")); } if sha256(split_source.as_bytes()).as_hex() != SPLITS_SHA256 { return Err(ReferenceHandoffError::FixtureMismatch("split manifest")); } // Safe callers obtain this opaque proof only through the foundation's // approved-manifest/compiled-census verification, not a revision string. let identity = reference_input_identity( &tiny_config_identity()?, corpus_source.as_bytes(), split_source.as_bytes(), source.identity(), )?; let digest = identity.digest()?; let observation = run_capstone( corpus_source, split_source, checkpoint_path, CapstoneConfig::tiny(), )?; let evaluation = observation.final_evaluation(); let checkpoint = observation.checkpoint(); if observation.training().parameter_count() != 1188 || observation.training().optimizer_step() != 32 || !observation.training().replay_bitwise() || evaluation.window_count() != 436 || evaluation.window_target_slot_count() != 1744 || evaluation.document_transition_occurrence_count() != 442 || !evaluation.decoder().mean_nll().is_finite() || !evaluation.bigram().mean_nll().is_finite() || !checkpoint.bytes_roundtrip() || !checkpoint.model_bits_exact() || !checkpoint.optimizer_bits_exact() || !checkpoint.tokenizer_exact() || !checkpoint.prompt_logits_bitwise() || !observation.generation().tokens_exact() || !observation.generation().decisions_bitwise() || !observation.generation().rng_state_exact() { return Err(ReferenceHandoffError::Invariant( "scalar reference handoff evidence changed", )); } Ok(ReferenceHandoffTrace { identity, digest, source_revision: source.source_revision().to_owned(), observation, }) } What matching identities do not prove A matching digest identifies the same canonical input record, subject to the hash’s collision-resistance assumption. It does not prove that the algorithm is correct or that a new machine will reproduce every floating-point bit. The source identity deliberately covers the forty scalar-reference source files, not this chapter’s reporting wrapper or interface. Toolchain, locked dependencies and arithmetic environment are recorded separately. A matching source digest is therefore not evidence that two execution environments match. The temporary checkpoint path is also outside the input identity; changing that path does not change the model’s fixed inputs. Likewise, exact checkpoint reload is narrower than complete job resumption. This check does not restore every data cursor, in-flight operation or whole-job continuation state. No laptop throughput is measured here.

reading.roleRequirement: State the two primary sources' supported reporting and variation claims with correct titles and chronology; separate same-seed replay from seed variability and compare the scalar getter with the scope-bearing report from one observation,without pretending to execute historical models.
reading.value: History: reporting conditions and measuring variation A language-model score without its input conditions and scope does not identify what was evaluated or establish which capabilities were checked. Model Cards for Model Reporting was presented in 2019. Mitchell and colleagues propose model documentation that includes intended uses and evaluation conditions; a model card is not itself proof of quality. Model Cards describe evaluation conditions and intended uses; later fine-tuning experiments study variation across initializations and data orders. Reporting scope and measuring variation answer different questions. In Fine-Tuning Pretrained Language Models: Weight Initializations, Data Orders, and Early Stopping, published in 2020, Dodge and colleagues study fine-tuning variability associated with initialization and data order for pretrained language models. This does not measure variability in the course’s tiny decoder. Keep a fixed regression reference when changing an LLM pipeline, while recording separately the evidence needed for quality, seed sensitivity and hardware claims. The Rust reporting contrast uses the same observation. Reading only the mean NLL with this expression gives a number: trace .observation() .final_evaluation() .decoder() .mean_nll() trace.report() also states the evaluation unit, input identity, replay accounting and limits. It does not retrain a historical model or execute a seed sweep. Report the same scalar observation with its metric unit, input identity and explicit capability limits. rust/demos/ch40-reference-core-handoff/src/lib.rs#scope-bearing-report /// Read structured evidence from this one observation; never parse stdout /// or run another model to produce either reporting projection. pub fn report(&self) -> Result<String, ReferenceHandoffError> { let run = &self.observation; let evaluation = run.final_evaluation(); let checkpoint = run.checkpoint(); let generation = run.generation(); let config = CapstoneConfig::tiny(); let targets_per_schedule = config.updates() * config.update_batch_size() * config.context_length(); let record = serde_json::json!({ "schema_version": 1, "chapter": "40-reference-core-handoff", "reference_identity": self.digest.as_hex(), "source_revision": self.source_revision, "scope": "scalar-reference-fixed-fixture-regression", "documents": { "train": run.partitions().train_document_ids().len(), "validation": run.partitions().validation_document_ids().len(), "test": run.partitions().test_document_ids().len() }, "model": { "parameters": run.training().parameter_count(), "context_tokens": config.context_length() }, "training": { "target_count_basis": "derived-from-frozen-full-batch-schedules", "updates_per_schedule": config.updates(), "independent_schedules": 2, "valid_targets_per_schedule": targets_per_schedule, "valid_targets_primary_plus_replay": 2 * targets_per_schedule, "selected_step": run.training().selected_step(), "within_invocation_replay_bitwise": run.training().replay_bitwise() }, "evaluation": { "unit": "overlapping-window-target-slot", "windows": evaluation.window_count(), "window_target_slots": evaluation.window_target_slot_count(), "document_transition_occurrences": evaluation.document_transition_occurrence_count(), "transition_multiplicity_counts": evaluation.transition_multiplicity_counts(), "decoder_mean_nll_nats_per_slot": evaluation.decoder().mean_nll(), "bigram_mean_nll_nats_per_slot": evaluation.bigram().mean_nll(), "once_per_transition_metric_reported": false, "independent_generalization_estimate": false }, "checkpoint": { "bytes_roundtrip": checkpoint.bytes_roundtrip(), "model_bits_exact": checkpoint.model_bits_exact(), "optimizer_bits_exact": checkpoint.optimizer_bits_exact(), "tokenizer_exact": checkpoint.tokenizer_exact(), "logit_probe_text": checkpoint.logit_probe_text(), "logit_probe_ids": checkpoint.logit_probe_ids(), "probe_logits_bitwise": checkpoint.prompt_logits_bitwise(), "complete_job_resume_established": false }, "generation": { "prompt": generation.prompt_text(), "token_ids": generation.generated_ids(), "decoded_text": generation.decoded_text(), "cached_reference_tokens_exact": generation.tokens_exact(), "cached_reference_decisions_bitwise": generation.decisions_bitwise(), "cached_reference_rng_exact": generation.rng_state_exact(), "useful_language_quality_established": false }, "laptop_throughput_measured": false, "successor_chapter": SUCCESSOR_CHAPTER }); let mut text = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&record) .map_err(|_| ReferenceHandoffError::Serialization)?; text.push('\n'); Ok(text) } Repeating seed 39 checks repeatability under fixed conditions. It does not estimate variability across seeds. Those are complementary checks, not interchangeable evidence.

reviewBundle.rubric:
# Technical and pedagogical criteria

Assess every supplied complete document, reading-order unit and isolated surface
against its frozen role requirement, supplied evidence and commitment map.
Repeat each requirement exactly in its assessment; do not narrow or replace it.

Check technical and mathematical truth, executable evidence, numerical units and
denominators, assumptions, conditions, actors, operations, causal relationships,
ordering, scope, limitations and excluded inferences. Distinguish observations,
derivations, course-local policies, proposals and future measurements. Copied
claims or matching projections are not independent executable evidence.

Check agreement among source, built content, formulas, Rust excerpts, recorded
outputs, diagrams, exercises, answers and handoffs. Judge whether explanations
make the required relationships understandable at the stated learner level.
Respect the declared revision scope without ignoring inconsistencies introduced
by the revision. Preserved material must not acquire a different meaning through
changed context.

Compare complete source and built documents with the inventory. Report omitted
or misclassified affected atoms, reading units, isolation groups and role
requirements against their owning complete-document surfaces. Check that each
frozen requirement covers the evidence-backed commitments for its actual role.
An audit-only extraction view provides exact values and provenance, not an
additional learner-facing source of context or proof.

Give each unit a substantive evidence-based rationale. Report unresolved source
ambiguity as a blocker rather than selecting a plausible interpretation. Apply
the output schema's severity and verdict rules consistently. A clean pass is

import ReferenceCoreHandoffDiagram from "../../../components/chapters/ReferenceCoreHandoffDiagram.astro";

export const diagramLabels = {
  title: "A reference identity is not a capability certificate",
  description: "The configuration, exact corpus and split bytes, and verified scalar-reference source determine the input identity. Separate checks observe replay, fixed-window evaluation, reload and cached generation. Neither the identity nor those checks establishes useful language quality, complete job resumption or laptop throughput.",
  inputs: "Identify the fixed inputs",
  checks: "Read the checked reference behavior",
  future: "Keep unmeasured capabilities separate",
  digest: "SHA-256 identity of the fixed input record",
  parameters: "Learned scalar parameters",
  slots: "Overlapping test-window target slots",
  transitions: "Within-document transition occurrences",
  generation: "Generated token IDs",
  limits: "Not established: useful language quality, complete job resumption or laptop throughput.",
};

{/* chapter-section:worked-example */}

## The problem: changes need a fixed comparison point

The previous chapter joined the tokenizer, decoder, training, evaluation,
checkpoint and generation code. Now the course will extend that system. If the
data, configuration and code change together, a changed result no longer tells
you which version you observed. You need a fixed reference that identifies its
inputs and states exactly what its checks establish.

This chapter keeps the small scalar decoder unchanged. It gives that reference
an input identity and a report whose claims stay attached to their evidence.
The identity identifies the fixed inputs. The checks establish which behavior
this execution reproduced. Neither establishes useful laptop-scale capability.

### What the reference actually does

The fixture assigns $8$ documents to training, $2$ to validation and $2$ to test.
The decoder has $1188$ learned scalar parameters and context capacity $4$ tokens.
Its primary training schedule and separately executed replay each perform $32$ updates
on full batches of $16$ windows, with $4$ valid targets per window. Therefore,
each schedule consumes

$$
32\cdot16\cdot4=2048
$$

valid training targets. One pipeline invocation includes both schedules: $4096$
targets altogether. These counts are derived from the frozen full-batch
schedule, not from a new runtime token counter. Evaluation targets and generated
tokens are separate quantities.

The report's `independent_schedules` field counts two separately executed copies
of the same schedule from training seed $39$, not statistically independent
seed samples.

The replay agrees bit for bit with the primary training result in this
execution. The selected decoder and frozen bigram then score the same $1744$
overlapping test-window target slots. Their mean negative log-likelihoods are
approximately $3.866087547$ and $3.981342714$ nats per slot, respectively.
This known comparison is a regression check: rerunning it can expose changes
in the checked behavior. It is not an independent estimate of generalization.

There are only $442$ within-document transition occurrences in those test
documents. Overlapping windows repeat occurrences, so $1744$ is not a count
of distinct transitions. A separate policy would score each occurrence once,
using the longest available causal prefix capped at four tokens and only its
newest-position distribution. This run does not report numeric mean NLL or
perplexity under that policy.

The checkpoint round trip preserves its encoded bytes, model and optimizer
bits, and tokenizer. The restored decoder reproduces logits for the fixed
`At` probe, encoded as token IDs `[67,118]`. Cached and complete-prefix generation
agree on token IDs `[260,34,34]`: Cyrillic `т` followed by two spaces. Agreement
checks the two generation paths; those three tokens do not demonstrate useful
language quality.

{/* chapter-section:formula */}

## The solution: identify inputs, then interpret evidence

$$
R_{\mathrm{ref}}=\operatorname{SHA256}(\mathrm{config}_{1188}\Vert\mathrm{fixture}\Vert\mathrm{source\_revision})
$$

{/* chapter-section:symbol-glossary */}

## The identity's symbols and fixed settings

$R_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is a $256$-bit digest, displayed as $64$ lowercase hexadecimal
characters. Its three named inputs are:

- $\mathrm{config}_{1188}$: a canonical record of eighteen tiny-run settings,
  together with the invariant that the decoder has $1188$ parameters.
- $\mathrm{fixture}$: a canonical record of SHA-256 digests of the exact corpus
  bytes and exact split-manifest bytes. Even a byte change that leaves parsed
  JSON meaning unchanged creates a different input identity.
- $\mathrm{source\_revision}$: a verified source identity combining a baseline
  revision with the exact forty course-owned scalar-reference source files.

Here $\Vert$ means composition into the shared identity format's named,
canonical fields, not writing three unframed strings beside one another.
That distinction matters: without field boundaries, different input sequences
can have the same concatenated bytes. The helper orders fields, serializes one
unambiguous record and hashes its complete bytes.

The settings fix eight BPE merges; decoder width, feed-forward width and context
capacity of four; one attention head and one block; stride one; training and
evaluation batch sizes of sixteen and one hundred twenty-eight; thirty-two
updates; learning rate $0.04$; gradient-norm cap $1$; training seed $39$;
generation seed $38$; bigram smoothing $1$; generation temperature $0.8$;
top-k four; and three generated tokens. The identity records floating-point
settings by their exact bit patterns rather than rounded display text.

<RustSource path="rust/demos/ch40-reference-core-handoff/src/lib.rs" region="reference-input-identity" caption="Bind configuration, exact fixture bytes and verified scalar-reference source to one input identity." label="Rust source: canonical scalar-reference input identity" />

The example verifies its compiled reference-source evidence first. It then
rejects changed corpus or split bytes before training or checkpoint work.
Only accepted fixed inputs reach the existing pipeline. The wrapper calls that
pipeline once; the pipeline itself performs primary training and replay.

<RustSource path="rust/demos/ch40-reference-core-handoff/src/lib.rs" region="reference-handoff" caption="Reject changed fixtures, run the unchanged scalar pipeline and retain only its checked observation." label="Rust source: fixed-fixture admission and scalar-reference execution" />

### What matching identities do not prove

A matching digest identifies the same canonical input record, subject to the
hash's collision-resistance assumption. It does not prove that the algorithm
is correct or that a new machine will reproduce every floating-point bit.

The source identity deliberately covers the forty scalar-reference source
files, not this chapter's reporting wrapper or interface. Toolchain, locked
dependencies and arithmetic environment are recorded separately. A matching
source digest is therefore not evidence that two execution environments match.
The temporary checkpoint path is also outside the input identity; changing
that path does not change the model's fixed inputs.

Likewise, exact checkpoint reload is narrower than complete job resumption.
This check does not restore every data cursor, in-flight operation or whole-job
continuation state. No laptop throughput is measured here.

{/* chapter-section:history */}

## History: reporting conditions and measuring variation

A language-model score without its input conditions and scope does not identify
what was evaluated or establish which capabilities were checked.

[Model Cards for Model Reporting](https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.03993v2) was
presented in 2019. Mitchell and colleagues propose model documentation that
includes intended uses and evaluation conditions; a model card is not itself
proof of quality.

Model Cards describe evaluation conditions and intended uses; later fine-tuning
experiments study variation across initializations and data orders. Reporting
scope and measuring variation answer different questions.

In [Fine-Tuning Pretrained Language Models: Weight Initializations, Data Orders, and Early Stopping](https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.06305v1),
published in 2020, Dodge and colleagues study fine-tuning variability associated
with initialization and data order for pretrained language models. This does
not measure variability in the course's tiny decoder.

Keep a fixed regression reference when changing an LLM pipeline, while recording
separately the evidence needed for quality, seed sensitivity and hardware claims.

The Rust reporting contrast uses the same observation. Reading only the mean
NLL with this expression gives a number:

```rust
trace
    .observation()
    .final_evaluation()
    .decoder()
    .mean_nll()
```

`trace.report()` also states the evaluation unit, input identity, replay
accounting and limits. It does not retrain a historical model or execute a seed
sweep.

<RustSource path="rust/demos/ch40-reference-core-handoff/src/lib.rs" region="scope-bearing-report" caption="Report the same scalar observation with its metric unit, input identity and explicit capability limits." label="Rust source: scope-bearing scalar-reference report" />

Repeating seed $39$ checks repeatability under fixed conditions. It does not
estimate variability across seeds. Those are complementary checks, not
interchangeable evidence.

{/* chapter-section:rust-implementation */}

## Run the reference without changing its inputs

The example obtains verified source evidence and owns its temporary checkpoint
location. Its report comes directly from the checked scalar observation, not
from parsing a previous human-readable report.

<RustSource path="rust/demos/ch40-reference-core-handoff/src/main.rs" region="reference-example" caption="Verify the reference source, use an owned temporary checkpoint and print the scope-bearing report." label="Rust source: executable fixed scalar-reference example" />

{/* chapter-section:visualization */}

## Keep the three evidence layers separate

The digest identifies the fixed inputs. The counts and generated token IDs
describe checked behavior on those inputs. The final card keeps future quality,
job-resumption and hardware claims outside the reference's evidence boundary.

<ReferenceCoreHandoffDiagram labels={diagramLabels} />

{/* chapter-section:exercises */}

## Optional practice: inspect the boundary

Run the example and inspect its report:

```sh
cargo run --quiet --locked -p ch40-reference-core-handoff
```

1. Find the identity, target-count basis and metric unit in the output. Explain
   why a digest alone would not replace the replay and reload checks.
2. Run the demo's tests. Identify the tests that change configuration, corpus,
   split bytes and source identity without training. Explain why constructing
   an identity for changed inputs does not admit them to the fixed reference run.
3. Explain why a successful checkpoint round trip cannot justify the statement
   “the complete training job can resume,” and why $1744$ must not be labeled
   “distinct test transitions.”

<details>
<summary>Answers: input identity, evidence scope and repeated target slots</summary>

1. The digest binds inputs; replay and reload compare actual behavior. Neither
   kind of evidence substitutes for the other. The target-count basis explicitly
   derives $2048$ targets per schedule and $4096$ for primary plus replay.
   The reported mean NLL uses nats per overlapping window-target slot.
2. The pure mutation tests construct different identities without calling the
   pipeline. The runner separately requires the exact accepted corpus and split
   bytes, so an identity is not an admission permit.
3. The checkpoint check covers persisted model, optimizer and tokenizer state
   plus a fixed logit probe, not every whole-job continuation dependency. The
   $1744$ denominator counts overlapping window-target slots; the underlying
   documents contain $442$ transition occurrences.

</details>

{/* chapter-section:decoder-connection */}

## What the next extension must preserve

You now have an identified scalar reference and a precisely bounded report.
A later change can be compared with that reference, while carrying its own
input identity and evidence. Chapter 41 will address governed corpus acquisition.
New data, larger models, accelerator execution, quality evaluation and complete
job resumption each require their own checks; none is already established by
this handoff.
